verified_claims: The task is fault mapping indicative of geothermal resources, not direct certification of a producing reservoir.
Distance-weighted Tversky uses alpha 0.2, beta 0.8 and a 300 m triangular kernel.
Submission requires a single float32 prediction band in [0,1] on the matching grid and CRS.
limits: A public problem-page read is not a portal validation or submission receipt.

verified_claims: Ranks and values in score_evidence.public_leaderboard_2026_10_22 were read directly from all three public leaderboard chunks.
limits: Public entries do not authenticate an artifact/score pairing and do not expose private submission-page receipts.

verified_claims: Staff says a new fault pixel absent from USGS/INGENIOUS can be an extension, splay, or parallel strand of an existing fault system; proximity alone is not proof of invalidity.
limits: This clarifies label scope, not the correctness of any local prediction.

official_sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey Earthquake Hazards Program
verified_claims: The current USGS overview describes the Quaternary Fault and Fold Database as documenting geologic evidence of coseismic surface deformation in large Quaternary earthquakes.
limits: Catalogue scope does not prove that a particular unmapped event cluster is a fault.

official_sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey ComCat FDSN Event Web Service
verified_claims: The documented API supports querying focal-mechanism products. For the sample-submission rectangle and 2000-01-01 through 2025-12-31, an M≥2.5 count query returned 5,886 events; adding producttype=focal-mechanism returned 2,249. A limited GeoJSON event query returned five records.
limits: Counts are remote API availability checks, not a locally ingested catalogue. The five records were not a complete export; focal mechanisms were not parsed, reprojected, or validated for spatial coverage.

verified_claims: The report abstract describes linear magnetic anomalies over alluvial deposits at Devils Hole and Pahrump Valley; spring alignments suggest concealed faults cutting alluvium and affecting groundwater. This is a regional analogy, not direct GeoDAWN-area validation.
limits: Only the first parsed chunk was read; the full report was not reviewed or downloaded as a local binary.

verified_claims: The report discusses reduction-to-pole, high-pass magnetic anomalies, susceptibility models and magnetite abundance; it notes magnetic response depends on magnetic minerals and field/local measurements vary by lithology. It is an environmental geophysical study in Montana, not a Great Basin fault-validation study.
limits: Selected parsed chunks were read; no complete report or local data were acquired.

official_sources.authority: U.S. Geological Survey ScienceBase Great Basin heat-flow item
verified_claims: Official ScienceBase JSON exposes a public downloadUri for the Great Basin heat-flow supporting-data ZIP (130,154,244 bytes; about 124.12 MiB). The release description identifies well-point residuals and says these may help identify hydrothermal or groundwater influence. The download link is publicly listed; no archive transfer is claimed.
limits: The ZIP bytes and advertised MD5 were not downloaded or locally verified; residual field names/units, coordinate quality, target-area well coverage, reuse details at file level, and residual QA were not independently checked in the archive.

official_sources.authority: Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem / Sentinel-1 STAC catalogue
verified_claims: Sentinel data are free, full and open under the Copernicus data terms; data download requires a registered user. The SLC collection describes complex I/Q pixels retaining phase; the bbox/date query returned five catalogue item records. One returned subswath asset is listed at 1,196,413,256 bytes (about 1.2 GB).
limits: No SLC assets were downloaded or hashed. The displayed sample footprint intersects the northeastern edge of the query rectangle; a complete target-footprint, track, repeat-cycle and interferometric-pair audit was not done. STAC discovery does not guarantee service availability or usable coherence.

official_sources.authority: U.S. Department of Energy Geothermal Data Repository
verified_claims: The public listing contains multiple Great Basin resources, including seismicity and geothermal context; its cited license is CC BY 4.0.
limits: No new GDR binary was acquired or hash-verified in this session.

official_sources.authority: Nevada Geodetic Laboratory, University of Nevada, Reno
verified_claims: The official MIDAS North America velocity text endpoint returned station records in the research fetch tool.
limits: Only response samples were read; no complete file, footprint-specific station count, hash, temporal coverage or spatial interpolation was verified.

The ScienceBase JSON exposes a public ZIP downloadUri and advertised byte size/MD5, but no binary was acquired or hash-verified. GDR resources were listed but not acquired; UNR MIDAS returned text samples only.
